title: Ancient Meteorite Found in the Sahara Holds Secrets About Mars’ Watery Past
gist: Teghaza 001, a meteorite of about two pounds found in the Sahara in 2022, is one of the oldest known pieces of Martian crust, at least 4.1 billion years old. Studies in Science and Science Advances found that its apatite crystals preserve hydrogen signatures from both Mars' interior and an ancient hydrosphere, evidence of early water-rock interaction.

insights.claim: Teghaza 001, a meteorite of about two pounds found in the Sahara in 2022, is a piece of Martian crust estimated to be at least 4.1 billion years old, making it one of the oldest known samples from Mars.
insights.speaker: Jorge Garay
insights.so_what: Rare ancient samples raise the scientific value of Mars research and sample collection.

insights.claim: Studies in Science and Science Advances found that, unlike most Martian meteorites, Teghaza 001 preserves chemical traces of interaction between the Martian crust and its ancient hydrosphere, and a reviewer called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars.
insights.speaker: Jorge Garay
insights.so_what: Adds evidence to the case for Mars habitability, a core rationale for Mars missions.
insights.quote: One of the paper’s reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars

insights.claim: Apatite crystals in the meteorite preserve two hydrogen signatures, one from Mars' interior and one from its ancient hydrosphere, showing material exchange between deep magma and a watery surface about 500 million years after the solar system formed.
insights.speaker: Jorge Garay
insights.so_what: Shows that water-rock interaction began very early on Mars, which bears on questions about early life.
insights.locator: Tiny crystals of a mineral called apatite

insights.claim: NASA scientist Lee Saper says the rock is the first piece of Martian crust from a region of Mars never sampled before and may record the Martian atmosphere as it lost water.
insights.speaker: Jorge Garay
insights.so_what: New sample diversity can change models of Mars' climate history.
insights.quote: This is really our first piece of Martian crust from a part of Mars we’ve never had a sample of before

insights.claim: The Sahara serves as a natural archive of Earth and solar system history, having also yielded 40-million-year-old fossils and, in 2019, a 4.5-billion-year-old fragment that may come from a vanished protoplanet possibly as large as the moon.
insights.speaker: Jorge Garay
insights.so_what: Desert meteorite recovery remains a low-cost source of planetary science data.

insights.claim: Explaining how Mars changed from having rivers and lakes to being cold and barren is part of the rationale for sending probes, rovers and perhaps crewed missions, but the article notes that answers sometimes arrive by chance as meteorites.
insights.speaker: Jorge Garay
insights.so_what: Unplanned sample finds can deliver science that complements expensive Mars missions.
insights.locator: Today, Mars is a cold and barren planet
